_readme: The framework of differences. Each dimension names one way the same clinical situation can be framed differently by a patient and by a clinician, how a turn is classified on it, which source-to-target contrasts its counterfactual step generates (each contrast is measured and reported under its own key; a source value with no contrast is observational only), and which probes can measure its effect. Dimensions and their values are owner-authored data: this file, never Python. Adding a dimension or a probe is a data change plus, for a probe, one adapter; tests/test_framework_schemas.py keeps the cross-references consistent. A probe's `inputs` say what a pair must carry before the probe may run; a pair lacking one is reported as unavailable for that probe, not measured with a default.

dimensions.name: Lexical register
dimensions.definition: Whether the situation is stated in everyday (colloquial) wording or in clinical terminology. The study's founding contrast.

counterfactual.note: A mixed turn has no single counterpart, so it is classified and judged but not re-elicited until the owner defines its contrast (candidate: rewrite to both poles, reported as two keys).

dimensions.name: <a second dimension, owner-authored>
dimensions.definition: <what differs between the two framings, stated so that a human annotator and a judge would agree on the boundary>

counterfactual.note: Every value must appear as the source of a contrast or in no_contrast.

dimensions.owner_notes: Replace or delete. Kept so the structure of a full entry is visible.

probes.name: Advice urgency tier and flags
probes.implementation: scripts/advice_eval.py judge (rubric data/advice_rubric.*.json); a judge-model call per turn, or human coding via scripts/advice_human_coding.py
probes.output: tier id plus flag ids per assistant turn

probes.name: Target-token probability difference
probes.completeness: batch_summary consumer: reject a summary with completed false or fewer results than pairs_requested, and emit a missing-index record per absent pair before analysis (medlang_circuits.batch_eval.run_batch truncates results on a mid-batch failure with no per-pair error record, AGENTS.md Architecture); a result whose screening.status is screened_out (the --screen-targets path: patient trace skipped, language_penalty null) is emitted as a named screened_out record and counted, never read as a measurement or dropped
probes.censoring: on logprobs_topn the target may be absent from the returned set: emit a named censored result for that side, never a probability (scripts/paired_stats.py already distinguishes the censored case)
probes.identity: exact target identity: the probability read is the persisted target's own, never a neighbour's. Where the adapter returns token ids, the scored id must equal the persisted id; where it returns token text only (the hosted path), the returned token unwrapped byte for byte (the hosted 'Output "..."' wrapper removed and nothing else: no whitespace stripping, no case folding, so a persisted leading space survives; medlang_circuits/targets.py bare_token strips and lowercases and is not that unwrap) must equal the persisted surface string exactly; a token that cannot be recovered byte for byte is target_identity_unverified. Any other match, including a prefix either way, is emitted as a named target_identity_unverified result for that side and counted, never a probability. The existing hosted path does not meet this: medlang_circuits/targets.py anchor_matches accepts a prefix match either way and target_probability returns the highest-probability match, which is the ' ant'/' anti' misread in AGENTS.md (Known measurement limitations); the framework adapter applies this rule on top of it until that path is changed, which re-publishes live numbers and is a separate decision

requires_levels.text_io: Any model reachable as text in, text out: every API and every product UI. The behavioural layer.
requires_levels.logits: Next-token probabilities for an explicit target token on both sides: open weights run locally, or an API that scores a named target.
requires_levels.activations: Forward-pass internals: open weights run locally.
requires_levels.hosted_graph: A hosted attribution-graph service that serves graphs for the model. Features are untagged unless hosted_graph_tagged also holds.
requires_levels.hosted_graph_tagged: hosted_graph plus a transcoder source set for the model, so features carry tags and clinical mass is meaningful.
requires_levels.hosted_lens: A hosted lens endpoint that serves readouts for the model (discovered per model by probing; not a local capability).
requires_levels.logprobs_topn: An API that returns only its top-N logprobs. Insufficient for logits: a probe listing logits may run here only with a named censored result whenever the target is absent from the returned set.

inputs_levels.pair_text: The two framings of the user turn plus the preceding context. Every pair has it.
inputs_levels.target_token: The clinical target token whose next-token probability the probe reads. Stimulus pairs carry it (target_clinical_token); a pair derived from an imported transcript has none until a target-selection rule (docs/framework_design.md section 3.4) assigns one and persists it in the pair record. The persisted value is per model: the surface string plus the token id actually scored, validated to be a single token in that model's tokenizer; a target that tokenises to more than one id is reported as target_not_atomic for that model, never scored on its first id (scripts/logits_eval.py build_result scores target_ids[0] only). Until a target is assigned, a probe that lists this input is reported as unavailable for that pair.
inputs_levels.response_text: The assistant reply for each arm of the pair, from one re-elicitation run under one pinned environment (docs/framework_design.md section 3.1). A pair whose re-elicitation was refused or failed on either arm lacks it and reports the response probes as unavailable by name, never judges a missing reply.

counterfactual_methods.translation: The study's patient-to-clinical translation step (advice_eval's translate request) and its reverse; recorded with the translator model version and the input/output sha256.
counterfactual_methods.manual: A human rewrites the turn; recorded with a role label and reviewed_utc.
counterfactual_methods.rule: A deterministic rewrite rule named and versioned in the adapter; recorded with the rule id.

reserved_annotation_values.not_applicable: Allowed as an annotation value on every dimension: the turn carries nothing to classify on it (an affirmation, a bare number, a person's name or a register-free identifier, an empty or attachment-only turn; a named diagnosis, medication, procedure or symptom carries register and is classified). Recorded as classification unavailable and counted, never guessed into a declared value; no contrast is generated for it. A dimension never lists it among its own values.
